svg.text: AWS Firecracker: MicroVM Guest-to-Host Breakout Anatomy (CVE-2026-5747 & CVE-2026-122192)
Virtio-PCI Device State Corruption, Memory Discard Desynchronization, and Jailer Boundaries
1. MicroVM Trust Boundaries
How Firecracker isolates untrusted multi-tenant workloads
The Rust VMM Architecture
• Ultra-minimal VMM (~50k LoC in Rust) using Linux KVM.
• Strips legacy PC devices: no BIOS, ACPI, or IDE.
• Emulates minimal virtio: net, block, vsock, balloon.
• Powers AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, Fly.io, and Koyeb.
Guest VM (Untrusted) <-- KVM --> Host VMM (Rust)
Transport: MMIO vs. Virtio-PCI
• Default Transport: virtio-mmio (memory-mapped I/O).
• Modern Opt-In: virtio-pci via --enable-pci.
• Virtio-PCI provides standard PCI BAR configurations
for modern high-performance cloud kernels.
virtio-pci: queue_sel, queue_size, queue_pfn
The Firecracker Jailer Sandbox
• Defense-in-depth wrapper executed before KVM init.
• Chroot: Locks process into isolated root directory.
• Cgroups: Limits CPU, RAM, and device nodes.
• Drops root: Runs as unprivileged user/group ID.
jailer --id vm1 --exec firecracker --uid 1000
Jailer Containment Outcome
• VMM heap corruption does NOT grant host root.
• Seccomp-BPF blocks execve, fork, and network.
• Attacker remains trapped in jailer chroot sandbox.
Result: Host kernel remains insulated.
2. Breakout Mechanisms (CVE Analysis)
Device state corruption and memory discard bugs
CVE-2026-5747: Virtio-PCI Out-of-Bounds Write
• Affected: Firecracker 1.13.0 - 1.14.3 and 1.15.0.
• Precondition: Attacker has root inside the guest VM.
• Flaw: Missing device activation check on PCI registers.
• Attack: Guest root writes to PCI queue registers AFTER
activation, mutating queue size & descriptor bounds.
vmm.virtio_pci.write_config(QUEUE_SIZE, malformed_val)
RESULT: VMM HEAP CORRUPTION / HOST ESCAPE
CVE-2026-122192: Memory Discard & Remap UAF
• Affected: Balloon and dynamic memory discard paths.
• Flaw: Guest inflates balloon or issues discard requests,
releasing host physical memory back to kernel.
• Race condition: VMM retains stale guest-physical to
host-virtual mappings for freed host pages (Use-After-Free).
madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) desynchronization
RESULT: MEMORY CORRUPTION / CROSS-VM LEAK
The Guest-to-Host Compromise Chain
1. Guest Kernel Ring 0 writes to virtio PCI BAR.
2. KVM VM-Exit routes I/O event to Firecracker VMM.
3. VMM corrupts internal heap state via OOB write.
4. Attacker redirects VMM execution to hijack host thread.
Guest Root -> VM-Exit -> VMM Heap -> Host Context
STATUS: VMM HIJACKED; CONTAINED AT JAILER
• Seccomp filter halts execve; host kernel uncompromised.
Defense-in-depth arrests hypervisor breakout.
3. Mitigation & Defenses
Patching versions and multi-layer isolation
Firecracker Security Patches
• Upgrade to Firecracker 1.14.4 or 1.15.1.
• Patch adds strict device state assertions:
if self.is_activated() {
error!("Cannot modify queue");
return;
• Prevents all post-activation mutations.
Immediate Operational Workaround
• If patching is delayed, disable virtio-pci.
• Revert to legacy virtio-mmio transport.
• Remove --enable-pci CLI parameter.
• Virtio-MMIO state machine is unaffected
by the PCI configuration register bug.
CLI: remove --enable-pci
The Rust Safety Boundary Paradox
• Firecracker is written in memory-safe Rust.
• Why did an OOB write occur?
1. State Machine Logic: Rust types cannot
prevent illegal sequence transitions.
2. Unsafe FFI & Memory Maps: Direct KVM
mmap & raw ring buffers require unsafe.
3. Lesson: Memory safety is not whole-system
correctness when managing devices.
State logic flaws bypass type safety.
• Multi-layer isolation is mandatory.
